a: Prefer O(1)/O(log n)/O(n) over O(n²) for large inputs; measure before micro-optimizing.
Premature optimization is tuning before you know the real bottleneck — profile first.
Profiling measures where time/memory is spent so you optimize the hot path.
Cache expensive results; set TTL; invalidate on writes; watch for stale data.
Fix N+1 queries with joins, batch fetches, or eager loading.
Prefer keyset/cursor pagination over large OFFSET for big tables.
Indexes help most on selective columns frequently used in WHERE/JOIN.
Lazy loading defers work until needed; can hurt if it causes many small loads.
Eager loading fetches related data upfront to avoid later round-trips.
CDNs cut latency by serving static assets from edge locations near users.
Compress HTTP responses (gzip/brotli) to reduce transfer size.
Pool DB/HTTP connections to avoid expensive connect/handshake per request.
Batch many small operations into fewer larger ones to cut overhead.
A memory leak retains unused memory — watch growing RSS and unbounded caches.
The hot path is the code executed most frequently; optimize it first.
Latency is time per request; throughput is requests per second — tune for your goal.
